title: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — Section 25 (Power to Make Rules)

content.overview: Section 25 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is the general power of the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act. Rules may provide for the matters enumerated in the section, including standards, hazardous substance procedures, prohibition or restriction on location of industries, procedures for entry and sampling, and form of notices. Section 25 is distinct from the more specific rule-making focus in s. 6 and is non-delegable under s. 23.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is there a Central rule under s. 25? (2) Does it carry out an Act purpose? (3) Interaction with s. 6 rules? (4) Non-delegable under s. 23?
content.study:
s. 25 is the general rule-making power. Always cite the specific rule/notification for numerical standards rather than inventing them.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: General rule-making
sections.body: Central Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act.

sections.heading: Enumerated subjects
sections.body: Includes standards of environmental quality, maximum allowable pollutant concentration, hazardous handling procedures, location restrictions, entry/sampling procedures and notice forms — as the section lists.

sections.heading: Link to s. 6
sections.body: s. 6 specifically authorises rules for matters referred to in s. 3; s. 25 is the broader carrying-out power. Both support subordinate environmental regulation.

sections.heading: Non-delegable
sections.body: s. 23 excludes s. 25 rule-making from delegation.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the rule, its statutory base and the obligation it creates on the facts.

examples.title: Procedural rule
examples.body: A Central rule under s. 25 prescribes the form of notice for sampling under s. 11 — compliance with that form supports valid sampling procedure.

hypotheticals.question: Can a State Government make EPA rules under s. 25?
hypotheticals.analysis: s. 25 vests rule-making in the Central Government and is non-delegable under s. 23.

distinctions.title: s. 25 general rules vs s. 6 pollution rules
distinctions.left: General power to make rules for carrying out the Act.
distinctions.right: Rules specifically for matters referred to in s. 3 (standards, hazardous procedures, location etc.).

misconceptions.trap: s. 25 and s. 6 are the same power.
misconceptions.correction: s. 6 is tied to s. 3 matters; s. 25 is the general rule-making power for the Act's purposes and is expressly non-delegable.
